macro.stance: Constructive demand, persistent physical bottlenecks, lower immediate Fed-hike risk but still-high input inflation.
marketContext: July PPI was unchanged month-over-month, reducing immediate September Fed-hike pressure.
Brent settled near $87 after a 2% pullback as a large U.S. crude inventory build and weaker demand forecasts offset continuing Hormuz risk.
U.S. electricity demand is still projected by EIA to set records in both 2026 and 2027, with AI/data centres a key driver.
macro.liveDesk: Latest cached Live Desk packet was generated 2026-08-13 and still marks AI/Data centres stale/neutral, so no conviction changes were taken from the overlay.

categoryReads.why: July ISM shows electrical-equipment and machinery expansion, too-low customer inventories, slower supplier deliveries and utility competition for electrical-equipment production slots. EIA electricity-demand forecasts remain structurally supportive.
actions: Maintain GEV, PWR, ETN, TNB and Dongfang Electric as priority names

categoryReads.why: ISM respondents describe active AI/data-centre procurement ramps and booming power/networking/photonics demand. Prefer power, electrical, cooling and network bottlenecks over adding more direct compute beta.
actions: Keep Southern Cable, YTL Power, SunCon, MN Holdings, nVent, Cloudflare and existing balance-of-system exposure under active review

categoryReads.why: BWXT continues to expand U.S. commercial nuclear manufacturing capacity and nuclear demand remains supported by power scarcity. No evidence today justifies rotating from operating/supplier exposure toward higher-risk reactor developers.
actions: Maintain BWXT, CEG and CGN Power preference over development-stage SMR beta

categoryReads.why: Domestic enrichment/HALEU scarcity remains strategic and Cameco retains integrated fuel-cycle advantages. No new daily evidence warranted changing LEU or CCJ scores.
actions: Maintain LEU and CCJ; watch execution and contracting rather than spot-price headlines

categoryReads.change: Slightly less aggressive on upstream; stronger on midstream/refining
categoryReads.why: Brent pulled back on a 17.4m-barrel U.S. crude build and weaker demand forecasts, while refining margins remain exceptionally strong because product supply is constrained. Gas infrastructure continues to benefit from LNG and power/data-centre load.
actions: Keep WMB and KMI high on gas-infrastructure list
Maintain MPC/VLO tactical refining preference but do not extrapolate record crack spreads indefinitely

categoryReads.why: Copper, electrical components, memory and semiconductors remain reported supply bottlenecks, but commodity pricing is volatile and tariff/geopolitical effects are distorting spot signals.
actions: Prefer bottleneck beneficiaries with pricing power over undifferentiated metal beta

categoryReads.why: Commercial evidence still favours warehouse/fixed automation first, then cobots/mobile manipulation, with humanoids remaining a later and more valuation-sensitive wave. Unitree's profitable IPO is useful evidence that humanoid economics are improving, but its extreme valuation does not overturn the adoption hierarchy.
actions: Keep SYM, Geekplus, CGNX and TER ahead of humanoid OEMs
Keep UBTECH as speculative humanoid exposure

companyChanges.reason: Q2 net sales +15%, organic +10%, adjusted EPS +12%; first-half Utility Solutions book-to-bill about 1.2x with transmission/substation order strength tied to load growth and data centres. Diversifies grid exposure beyond turbines and switchgear.

Q2 orders +88% organically, backlog +$13bn sequentially, data-centre orders above $5bn YTD and gas equipment commitments reached 116 GW. Thesis remains strongly validated; valuation is the primary restraint.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA +12% to a record second-quarter level and natural-gas transport volumes rose materially. Higher power/LNG demand plus the Western Gateway project improve visibility.
Momentum Midstream acquisition deepens Haynesville/LNG exposure and new pipeline projects extend growth, but Q2 earnings were slightly below expectations and acquisition/integration risk rose.
Q2 worldwide production +20%, Hess synergies ahead of plan, record U.S. production/refinery throughput and a 20-year Microsoft power agreement add a credible AI-power crossover.
U.S. refiners are capturing unusually strong product margins and returning substantial capital, but the setup is cyclical and crack spreads can normalise quickly if supply disruptions ease.

noChangeCoverage: All other existing Power Stack names were reviewed at category and catalyst level. No additional thesis, conviction or status changes cleared the materiality bar today.

notPromoted.reason: Commercially credible and profitable, but 219x projected 2025 earnings at IPO is too valuation-sensitive for a priority position and it remains outside the preferred HK/MY/US market set.
Current shortages are real, but existing Power Stack infrastructure names capture the bottleneck with less commodity-price dependence.
